identity.title: Application of AI-designed OpenCRISPR-1 for highly efficient gene editing in soybean (Glycine max L.) and Nicotiana benthamiana.

content.abstract: The widespread application of CRISPR/Cas genome editing for commercial crop improvement is currently hindered by a complex and restrictive intellectual property (IP) landscape. The recent development of OpenCRISPR-1, a fully AI-designed Cas9-like nuclease, provides a promising alternative with an accessible licensing framework; however, its efficacy in dicotyledonous plants remains largely uncharacterized. Here, we report the successful adaptation of the OpenCRISPR-1 system for targeted mutagenesis in soybean (Glycine max L.) and Nicotiana benthamiana. We constructed a plant-optimized binary vector (pBSE-OpenCRISPR-1) and validated its editing capability. In soybean (Glycine max), an Agrobacterium rhizogenes-mediated hairy root transformation assay targeting the GmFAD2-1B gene demonstrated that OpenCRISPR-1 actively induces site-specific mutations. In Nicotiana benthamiana, stable Agrobacterium-mediated transformation targeting the phytoene desaturase homologs (NbPDSa/b) achieved overall editing in 75% of T(0) transgenic lines (27/36). Analysis of individual homologs revealed editing rates of 66.7% (24/36) at both the NbPDSa and NbPDSb loci. Complete editing of the target locus occurred in 13.9% of events for NbPDSb and 2.8% for NbPDSa, including one event (2.8%) displaying simultaneous complete editing across all alleles resulting in a visible albino phenotype. Deep amplicon and Sanger sequencing revealed a characteristic mutation profile dominated by small insertions and deletions occurring two to three nucleotides upstream of the PAM. These results demonstrate that the AI-designed OpenCRISPR-1 system is a highly active and versatile nuclease for dicot genome engineering. By providing expanded freedom-to-operate, this tool broadens access to crop trait improvement worldwide.
